sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203], while operating income grew faster at 12.3% [F204] and net income at 14.7% [F205].
The window is a steady compounder with two step changes: revenue rose 17.5% in FY2021 [D189] and 15.8% in FY2022 [D238], against 5.0% in FY2024 [D336].
FY2021's jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase, with e-commerce comparable sales up 44% and gasoline price and volume adding to net sales [P54][P55].
FY2022's 16% net sales increase was driven by 14% comparable sales and strength in gasoline, business centers and travel, with inflation higher than prior years [P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue [D670] and 7.2pp of growth [D672], with Other International adding 1.6pp [D679] and Canada 1.3pp [D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, 10%, mainly on an 8% comparable sales increase from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue [D558] but contributed only 2.6pp of growth [D560], while warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp [D601].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026 [D435][D434], an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D457].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% in FY2026 [D438] against 13.9% net income growth [D436], as the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [X100].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026 [F32], its window high [D691] and 0.5pp above the 3.4% median [D692], though it sits at the 17th percentile of retail peers against a 5.0% median [D709][D710].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp [D447], with SG&A adding 0.1pp [D460] and cost of revenue flat [D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, but excluding gasoline price inflation it rose 10 basis points, helped by IEEPA tariff refunds of three basis points [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% [F52] trails operating margin by 0.8pp [D732], with the 24.7% effective tax rate [D420] the main below-the-line drag.
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026 [F82][D421], above the 1.75x window median [D722], and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income [F102][D422].
The FY2026 operating cash increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% [D418], above the 2.8% window median [D698] but at the 50th peer percentile against a 4.2% median [D713][D714].
Capex was 2.1% of revenue [D417] and 2.41x D&A [D423], the highest ratio in the window, as the warehouse build-out accelerated.
Net cash reached $15.1 billion in FY2026 [D427], 5.0% of revenue [D428], the 100th percentile of four retail peers against a -18.3% median [D733][D734].
Total debt was $6.2 billion [D426] against $21.3 billion of cash and investments [D425], and the current ratio was 1.06x [F182].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion consumed 35.2% of free cash flow [D429][D430], with $848 million of repurchases [X110] under a program with $1,115 million remaining [P3].
The diluted share count fell 0.1% in FY2026 [D452], so EPS growth tracked net income growth rather than exceeding it.
Operating margin of 3.9% [F32] is thin against the 5.0% retail peer median [D710], leaving little cushion if merchandise costs or wages rise faster than sales.
Capex has grown 11.1% a year over the window [F209], faster than the 9.3% free cash flow CAGR [F210], lifting capex to 2.41x D&A [D423].
The current ratio of 1.06x [F182] sits near the 1.02x window median [D704], and current liabilities grew 18.4% in FY2026 [D446] against 10.1% revenue growth [D434].
Operating margin: a print above the FY2026 high of 3.9% [D691] would confirm the multi-year grind higher, while a fall back to the 3.4% median [D692] would reverse it; watch the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow margin: holding above the 2.8% window median [D698] would confirm the cash trend, while a drop toward the 1.5% FY2022 low [D696] would signal capex outrunning cash generation.
Net cash: staying above the FY2026 level of $15.1 billion [D427] would confirm the balance-sheet build, while a fall toward the FY2024 $5.2 billion [D329] would mark a shift in capital allocation.
